session_summary: All seven stages are now built. Stage 5: bootstrap.py + INSTALL.bat/run.bat/install.command/run.command (venv, pinned packages, Chromium, Tk check, Desktop shortcut, install_state.json, quiet repair on every launch), fanout/updater.py (GitHub Releases check, SHA-256, backup, swap, package refresh, automatic rollback; frozen builds open the download page), update banner and Settings dialog (timing, be gentle, updates, repair, open logs/results). Stage 6: pyproject (ruff, pytest), CI on Windows/macOS/Linux, PyInstaller folder specs, release workflow, issue template, README, LICENSE (MIT), CHANGELOG, docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md, safety and no-traceback tests. Stage 7: nothing private is tracked; pushed to main; tag v0.2.0. PROVEN: ruff clean; 177 tests pass on ubuntu and macos, 176 + 1 skipped on windows, in GitHub Actions run 45990579939, which also ran the real Tk tests and `app.py --smoke-test` (first screen = brave-missing on all three). A real update ran offline in a real venv against a fake GitHub (swap, refresh, rollback). Real bugs found by CI and fixed: helper threads holding the Tk app (macOS abort), Tk objects freed on the wrong thread, Linux-only path assumptions in two Stage 1/2 tests (Windows). NOT proven: real Brave, real chat sites, INSTALL.bat/install.command on a clean machine, PyInstaller builds, the update banner and Settings dialog in a real window by eye, the macOS/Windows login-import and tiling with real screens. Stage 7 is PARTIAL: everything is pushed to main and nothing private is tracked, but this session's GitHub policy denied pushing the v0.2.0 tag (HTTP 403) and writing repo description/topics, so neither was done; the release workflow now also fills in a release the user starts by hand. Code review pass (Opus): fixed a possible double send on sites that clear the chat box slowly (real-browser test fails without the fix), routed helper errors by command instead of always jumping to Scan, made a dead helper fail at once, kept history-save failures from blocking runs, made Windows 'Close Brave for me' target only the person's Brave by PID, reaped leftover browsers before deleting temporary copies, limited update downloads to https, fixed a pyright type error. Easy-install pass: added FanOut icon (window, exe, installer, shortcuts), one-file Windows installer FanOut-Setup-x.y.z.exe (Inno Setup, per-user, no admin, Desktop+Start menu shortcuts, uninstaller, Chromium inside, no headless shell), installed-app self-update via the new installer (SHA-256 checked, silent install, reopens), app.py --self-test. PROVEN on GitHub's Windows runner (job windows-installer, run 46004198639): silent install, shortcuts, Apps & features entry, installed app's Chromium starts, window opens, upgrade over the top, data kept, uninstall removes program and shortcut and keeps data. Sizes 176.9 MB installer, 570.1 MB installed.
last_verified_step: GitHub Actions run 46004198639 on commit 36c5da4: lint, tests on windows/macos/ubuntu, and windows-installer (14 checks: install, shortcuts, self-test, smoke-test, update over the top, data kept, uninstall) all green.

deviations_kept: Mapping scripts live in fanout/js/ (inside the package) so they ship with it; PyInstaller specs in Stage 6 must include them as data
Stage 3 was built before Stages 1 and 2 are verified_done, at the user's request; Stage 1 stays the current stage
Send-button/reply selectors are detected after typing the test word, because many sites only show Send once there is text; the dry run never clicks it
Stage 4 was built before Stages 1-3 are verified_done, at the user's request; Stage 1 stays the current stage
Checklist items 7, 8, 9, 11, 12 are PASS on local fake chat sites in headless Chrome only; they still need one run on real chat sites with real Brave
Reply selector is looked for again after sending when none is saved, because the reply area often does not exist before the first reply
Stages 5, 6 and 7 were built before Stages 1-3 were proven on a real machine, at the user's request ('Finish all stages'); every stage stays in_progress until real-machine proof
bootstrap.py is at the repo root and uses only the standard library, so INSTALL.bat can run it before the venv exists
ruff line length is 140 (existing code was written to ~120-130), rules E,F,I,B,UP,SIM,RUF100
The Release is published by the release workflow (GITHUB_TOKEN); the local gh token is invalid, so repo description and topics are set through the REST API
A release publishes its source zip + SHA-256 even if a packaged build fails, because in-app updates depend only on those two files

Windows users install with a one-file Inno Setup installer (FanOut-Setup.exe) instead of INSTALL.bat, to match the user's other apps; INSTALL.bat stays as the run-from-source route. The installed app updates by running the new installer silently instead of swapping files
blockers: Tag push and repo description/topics were denied by this session's GitHub policy (403); they need the user (Releases page and the About gear). Not retried or worked around
Real Brave, real chat sites and a real Windows 11 desktop are needed for the Stage 1, 2, 3 exit proofs; the sandbox has none
INSTALL.bat on a clean Windows PC with no Python is UNTESTED (manual steps are in the README); install.command on a clean Mac/Linux is UNTESTED
Update banner, Settings dialog and results screen appearance have never been looked at in a real window by a person (tests drive them, nobody has seen them)
Mode B (reuse real Brave profiles) risk: newer Chromium may refuse automation on the default user data folder; unverified with real Brave
The installer is not code-signed (signing needs a paid certificate), so Windows SmartScreen shows 'More info > Run anyway' on first install
safety_baseline: Tracked files are code, tests, .gitignore and FANOUT_STATE.json only. .gitignore excludes sessions/ browser_profile/ config.json results/ logs/ .venv/ install_state.json .backup/ dist/ build/. App data (config, sessions, logs) lives in the per-user app data folder, outside the repo. Login import copies only Network/Cookies(+journal), Preferences and Local State.
